The 240 IPIP-HEXACO items and their keys

Source: R/data.R
hexaco_items.Rd

The items of hexaco_real and hexaco_llm in their original order, with the trait and facet each one measures and whether it is reverse-keyed. Each of the six traits has four facets of 10 items; 122 items are reverse-keyed.

Usage

hexaco_items

Format

A data frame with 240 rows and 7 columns: item (column name in the response data), trait (H, E, X, A, C or O), trait_label (for example Honesty-Humility), facet and facet_label (for example HSinc and Sincerity), statement (the item text) and reverse (TRUE for reverse-keyed items).

Source

International Personality Item Pool (public domain), https://ipip.ori.org; see Ashton, Lee & Goldberg (2007) in hexaco_real.

See also

hexaco_real, hexaco_llm.

Examples

table(hexaco_items$trait_label, hexaco_items$reverse)
#>                         
#>                          FALSE TRUE
#>   Agreeableness             15   25
#>   Conscientiousness         21   19
#>   Emotionality              25   15
#>   Extraversion              23   17
#>   Honesty-Humility          12   28
#>   Openness to Experience    22   18
head(hexaco_items[, c("item", "facet_label", "statement", "reverse")])
#>     item facet_label
#> 1 HSinc1   Sincerity
#> 2 HSinc2   Sincerity
#> 3 HSinc3   Sincerity
#> 4 HSinc4   Sincerity
#> 5 HSinc5   Sincerity
#> 6 HSinc6   Sincerity
#>                                                                                 statement
#> 1                                                   I don't pretend to be more than I am.
#> 2                                                            I use flattery to get ahead.
#> 3 I tell other people what they want to hear so that they will do what I want them to do.
#> 4                                                      I put on a show to impress people.
#> 5                                              I switch my loyalties when I feel like it.
#> 6                                               I play a role in order to impress people.
#>   reverse
#> 1   FALSE
#> 2    TRUE
#> 3    TRUE
#> 4    TRUE
#> 5    TRUE
#> 6    TRUE
